title: Per-IP auth rate limiter collapses to one shared bucket behind a reverse proxy (login DoS + brute-force bypass)
detail: resolve_ip() prefers the transport peer from ConnectInfo and consults X-Forwarded-For ONLY when there is no peer. With into_make_service_with_connect_info the peer is ALWAYS present, so behind a reverse proxy / TLS terminator (the documented 'on Hetzner the env comes from compose' deployment) the peer is the proxy's address for every request. The limiter therefore buckets the entire internet under one IP: (a) any single client can spend the global budget (default 10 attempts / 60s) and lock out every user's login/register/yggdrasil-authenticate/refresh — a trivial DoS; (b) an attacker on a different source IP cannot be isolated or throttled relative to legitimate users, defeating brute-force protection. The code comment even acknowledges XFF 'must only be reachable behind a proxy that overwrites X-Forwarded-For,' but the logic only reaches XFF when ConnectInfo is absent — the opposite of what a proxied deployment needs.
fix: Make proxy-awareness explicit and configurable: add a TRUSTED_PROXY flag (or trusted CIDR list). When set, derive the client IP from the right-most/known-good hop of X-Forwarded-For (or a proxy-set header like X-Real-IP) instead of the transport peer; when unset, use the peer as today. Never trust XFF unless behind a configured trusted proxy. Document that the limiter is per-client only when the proxy header is trusted.

title: /metrics is unauthenticated and exposes operational telemetry
detail: GET /metrics is mounted at the root with no AuthUser/AdminUser guard and no IP/network restriction, returning Prometheus counters and live gauges (bootstraps, heartbeats, friend requests, join tickets, relay sessions/bytes forwarded, signaling connections, active relays, connected users). This leaks real-time network activity and usage volume to any anonymous caller and gives an attacker a free oracle for sizing/timing attacks and reconnaissance. /health (infra.rs:13-30) similarly reveals DB up/down to anyone, though that is lower value.
fix: Gate /metrics behind AdminUser (or a dedicated metrics token), or bind it to a separate internal listener / restrict by source network at the proxy. If a scrape target must stay token-free, at minimum restrict it to the metrics network. Consider returning only a minimal status from /health to anonymous callers.
area: Backend security audit — loontail-minecraft-network-service (crates: core, server, catalog, bundles, textures, yggdrasil, yggdrasil-protocol, network, admin)

title: Rate limiter fails OPEN and falls back to client-controllable X-Forwarded-For
detail: When no IP can be resolved the middleware runs next.run() unthrottled (fail-open), and the only IP fallback path parses the first hop of the client-supplied X-Forwarded-For header. In any environment where ConnectInfo could be absent (or if SEC-1 is 'fixed' naively by trusting XFF), an attacker sets X-Forwarded-For to a rotating/forged value to get a fresh bucket per request, bypassing the limiter entirely. This is the mirror risk of SEC-1: today XFF is only reached without a peer, but the header remains attacker-controlled.
fix: Only ever derive an IP from XFF behind a configured trusted proxy (see SEC-1). When the IP genuinely cannot be resolved on a credential path, prefer fail-closed (or a conservative global cap) rather than unthrottled passthrough, since these are exactly the endpoints worth protecting.
area: Backend security audit — loontail-minecraft-network-service (crates: core, server, catalog, bundles, textures, yggdrasil, yggdrasil-protocol, network, admin)

title: Open public self-registration creates confirmed accounts with no email verification or registration abuse controls
detail: POST /api/auth/register creates a usable, confirmed='true' Yggdrasil account from arbitrary username/email with no email ownership verification and no controls beyond the shared IP rate limit (which is undermined by SEC-1). An attacker can mass-create accounts (resource/username-squatting, spam of friend requests, polluting user search) and bind arbitrary unverified emails. The code comment marks this an MVP choice, but it is an attack surface worth gating before exposure.
fix: Add email-confirmation (set confirmed=false until verified) or at least a registration-specific throttle/captcha and per-email/per-IP caps that survive a proxy. Validate email format and consider disposable-domain blocking.

title: Yggdrasil access/client tokens are stored and compared in plaintext at rest
detail: Unlike session tokens (hashed via hash_token), the Yggdrasil pair is persisted as 64-hex plaintext and looked up with WHERE access_token = $1. A read-only DB compromise (backup leak, SQLi elsewhere, log of a row) immediately yields usable in-game credentials for up to the 15-day TTL. The module documents this as protocol-mandated (the Mojang client echoes the token verbatim), which is a legitimate constraint, so this is a residual-risk note rather than a clear-cut bug. Token entropy (256-bit) means the equality lookup is not a practical timing oracle.
fix: Where feasible, store a keyed hash (HMAC) of the access token and look up by that, keeping the plaintext only in transit; or at minimum ensure DB-at-rest encryption, tight row-level access, and that tokens are never written to logs. Keep the per-user cap (already present) and short TTL.
area: Backend security audit — loontail-minecraft-network-service (crates: core, server, catalog, bundles, textures, yggdrasil, yggdrasil-protocol, network, admin)

title: Bundles admin file operations rely solely on DB existence, not validate_slug, before filesystem joins
location: crates/bundles/src/admin.rs:118-128 (delete -> delete_build_files), :134-186 (upload_archive -> tempfile_for/ensure_build_dir), :251-366 (upload_file), and other handlers using files_path(root,&slug); contrast public path which calls storage::validate_slug (crates/bundles/src/public.rs:27-29,63)
detail: Admin handlers take {slug} and feed it straight into filesystem paths (delete_build_files, files_path, tempfile_for) after only repo::require_by_slug (a DB lookup). This is not currently exploitable because slugs are validated at creation (provision_bundle_row calls validate_slug, crates/bundles/src/repo.rs:59) so a traversal slug cannot exist as a row, and require_by_slug 404s otherwise. It is a defense-in-depth gap: the public handlers defend with validate_slug + canonicalize-contain, but the admin handlers omit the explicit slug guard and the canonicalize-contain re-check, leaning entirely on the DB invariant.
fix: Call storage::validate_slug(&slug) at the top of every admin handler that touches the filesystem (mirroring public::serve_file/get_manifest) so the FS guard does not depend on the DB-uniqueness invariant holding forever.
area: Backend security audit — loontail-minecraft-network-service (crates: core, server, catalog, bundles, textures, yggdrasil, yggdrasil-protocol, network, admin)

title: CSRF double-submit compare is non-constant-time and the token lives in a JS-readable cookie
location: crates/core/src/auth/csrf.rs:34-44 (verify_csrf, cookie != header), :13 (CSRF cookie not httpOnly by design)
detail: verify_csrf compares the cookie and header with a plain != on attacker-influenceable values; while a timing oracle here is weak (the CSRF token is delivered to the legitimate same-origin SPA and an attacker generally controls only the header, not the matching cookie), constant-time comparison is the conventional hardening for token checks. The double-submit pattern is otherwise sound (httpOnly session cookie + readable CSRF cookie + SameSite=Lax + explicit CSRF allowlisted header in CORS).
fix: Use a constant-time comparison (e.g. subtle::ConstantTimeEq or ring::constant_time) for the cookie==header check. Optionally bind the CSRF token to the session (HMAC over the session id) so a stolen-but-stale CSRF cookie cannot be reused across sessions.
area: Backend security audit — loontail-minecraft-network-service (crates: core, server, catalog, bundles, textures, yggdrasil, yggdrasil-protocol, network, admin)

title: Security headers (CSP/HSTS/nosniff/frame/referrer) are scoped only to /admin, leaving other responses bare
detail: HSTS, X-Content-Type-Options, X-Frame-Options, CSP and Referrer-Policy are applied only to the admin subtree. JSON/error responses and the file-serving routes (textures PNGs, bundle files, catalog media) carry none — notably no nosniff and no HSTS. The intent (don't alter binary file responses) is reasonable, but nosniff and HSTS are safe and valuable across the whole origin; their absence on file routes allows MIME-sniffing-based content confusion on user-uploaded bytes (skins, catalog media, bundle files served with attacker-influenced extensions) and leaves non-admin TLS without HSTS. CSP also permits style-src 'unsafe-inline' (documented react-aria tradeoff).
fix: Apply X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff (and HSTS) globally at the outer router, keeping the stricter CSP/frame headers admin-scoped. Ensure user-uploaded file routes always send a correct, fixed Content-Type plus nosniff so a .html/.svg upload cannot be rendered in-origin.
area: Backend security audit — loontail-minecraft-network-service (crates: core, server, catalog, bundles, textures, yggdrasil, yggdrasil-protocol, network, admin)

title: Bootstrap admin seeded with a fixed synthetic email and password from env; promotion of any existing same-named user
detail: ensure_bootstrap_admin will, when no admin exists, PROMOTE any pre-existing user holding the bootstrap username (default 'admin') to is_admin=true/confirmed=true, and otherwise create an admin with email {normalized}@admin.local and the env password. Two risks: (1) if an attacker can register the username 'admin' before first admin bootstrap on a fresh deploy, a later bootstrap promotes that attacker-controlled account to admin; (2) a weak/committed ADMIN_BOOTSTRAP_PASSWORD yields an admin login. The last-admin guard protects against lockout but not against this seeding path.
fix: Do not auto-promote an arbitrary existing account by username; require an explicit, dedicated bootstrap that fails if the username is already taken (or match on a known marker). Enforce a strong bootstrap password (length/complexity check at startup) and document rotating it after first login.

title: TraceLayer logs full request URIs; WebSocket/relay token fallback travels in the query string
detail: The signaling and relay WS upgrades accept the session/ticket token via a ?token= query parameter as a fallback to the Bearer header. TraceLayer::new_for_http() logs request method+path/URI at its default span; with default span config the path (including query) can be emitted to logs, and the query is also routinely captured by upstream proxies/access logs. A leaked log line thus discloses a live session token or single-use join ticket. The request-log sink correctly stores only the matched-route template (not the raw query), but the tracing layer and any fronting proxy do not.
fix: Prefer the Bearer header for WS auth and, if a query fallback must remain, redact 'token' from any URL before it reaches tracing/proxy logs (custom TraceLayer make_span that strips the query, and proxy log config that drops query strings). Single-use tickets already limit blast radius; session tokens via ?token= are the bigger concern.

title: Friend queries decode nullable users.minecraft_uuid as non-nullable String → 500 for credential-only friends
detail: Migration 0003 (migrations/0003_identity.sql) drops NOT NULL on users.minecraft_uuid; accounts created via /api/auth/register (crates/core/src/identity.rs register_user) or admin_create_user without a minecraft_uuid carry NULL. FriendRequestRow and FriendPresenceRow declare minecraft_uuid as `String` (not Option<String>). The SELECTs in FRIEND_REQUEST_SELECT (friends.rs:88) and friends_with_presence (presence.rs:252) select `u.minecraft_uuid`; sqlx fails to decode NULL into String, returning sqlx::Error -> AppError::Database -> HTTP 500. So GET /friends, GET /friends (presence), GET /friends/requests/incoming|outgoing, and friend accept/decline DTO assembly all break the moment a friend (or requester/target) is a credential-only user. Tests pass only because seed_user always bootstraps a minecraft_uuid first (crates/network/tests/network_api.rs:95-108). Note users::search already correctly uses Option<String> (crates/network/src/users.rs:147), confirming the column is nullable.
fix: Change from_minecraft_uuid/to_minecraft_uuid in FriendRequestRow and minecraft_uuid in FriendPresenceRow to Option<String>, and set UserDto.minecraft_uuid = row.from_minecraft_uuid (drop the Some(...) wrapper) in the From impls / mappers. Same change anywhere a *_minecraft_uuid is read into String from the users table for a non-bootstrap-guaranteed user.

title: Skin/cape rows keyed by user_id but read by profile_uuid; reconcile changes profile_uuid without updating textures → texture silently lost
location: crates/textures/src/handlers.rs:37,48,74 (lookup/read_png query WHERE profile_uuid=$1); crates/core/src/identity.rs:308-322 (assign_or_reconcile_profile_uuid only UPDATEs users); migrations/0005_textures.sql (skins/capes store a denormalized profile_uuid)
detail: skins/capes PK is user_id and they store a denormalized profile_uuid captured at upload time (handlers.rs upsert binds &profile_uuid). lookup() and read_png() resolve by profile_uuid, and yggdrasil profile assembly (crates/yggdrasil/src/profile.rs load_skin/load_cape) resolves by user_id. A credential-only user (random profile_uuid) who uploads a skin, then bootstraps with a minecraft_uuid, has users.profile_uuid rewritten to undash(minecraft_uuid) by reconcile_profile_uuid/assign_or_reconcile_profile_uuid — but the skins/capes row still holds the OLD profile_uuid. After that, GET /textures/{newUuid} and the launcher's textures lookup find no row (the skin appears deleted), while the signed GameProfile (built by user_id) still references it — an inconsistent, surprising state.
fix: Either (a) make profile_uuid authoritative only in users and have textures lookups join skins/capes via users.id (e.g. lookup by joining users ON users.profile_uuid=$1 then skins.user_id=users.id), or (b) update skins.profile_uuid and capes.profile_uuid inside assign_or_reconcile_profile_uuid when the user's profile_uuid changes. Option (b) is the smallest fix: add `UPDATE skins SET profile_uuid=$2 WHERE user_id=$1` and same for capes in the same path.

title: PATCH /world-sessions/:id status='closed' skips relay/presence/player-count cleanup that DELETE performs
detail: close() runs a transaction that, besides marking the world closed, resets the host's presence to online + nulls current_world_session_id and sets all the world's relay_sessions to 'closed'. update() lets a host set status='closed' (worlds.rs:110) but only writes the world row's status/closed_at — it does NOT close relay sessions or reset host presence/current_players. So closing a world via PATCH leaves dangling 'active' relay rows (which keep guests falsely in-world for friend-of-friends visibility via friends_with_presence LATERAL and is_friend_of_active_member) and leaves the host's presence pointing at a closed world. current_players is also left non-zero.
fix: On update() when the new status is 'closed' and the prior status was 'open', run the same cleanup as close() (close relay_sessions for the world, reset host presence to online + null current_world_session_id, zero current_players) inside the existing/added transaction. Best: factor close()'s cleanup into a shared helper and call it from both.

title: Relay rendezvous park() overwrites an existing waiting peer and does not match by role → leaked socket / host-host pairing
location: crates/network/src/relay.rs:199-214 (handle_relay None branch) and crates/core/src/realtime.rs:184-189 (RelayHub::park uses HashMap::insert)
detail: park() does `waiting.insert(relay_session_id, peer)`. If a second 'first party' for the same relay_session_id arrives before the peer (e.g. the host reconnects the relay socket after a transient drop, or opens it twice), the existing parked PendingPeer is silently replaced; the replaced socket's done_tx is dropped and its task only unblocks at the 90s RENDEZVOUS_TIMEOUT. take() also matches purely on relay_session_id with no role check, so two host connections (both pass the host auth at relay.rs:83-88) can be paired host-to-host (the guest ticket is single-use, so guest-guest is prevented by validate_guest_ticket consuming the ticket). The capacity gate still applies, so impact is limited to a wasted/misrouted tunnel, not a capacity bypass.
fix: Record the role of the parked party and require take() to pair only opposite roles (host<->guest); on a same-role second arrival, refuse with a Conflict rather than overwriting. At minimum, have park() refuse (return the peer) when an entry already exists instead of insert-overwriting.

title: Catalog client listing is heavily N+1 (per-client: locale + media + keywords + per-keyword title + servers + bundle)
location: crates/catalog/src/repo.rs:317-353 (list_clients/list_clients_admin loop) calling build_client_dto:279-314, which calls client_locale/client_media/client_keywords (+ per-keyword keyword_title:209)/client_servers/bundle_summary
detail: GET /api/clients and admin GET /clients run 1 query for the client list, then for EACH client 5+ queries, and within client_keywords another query PER keyword for its localized title. With K clients each having N keywords this is roughly K*(5+N)+1 round-trips. Functionally correct but a latency/connection-pool hazard (pool max_connections=10, db.rs:11) as the catalog grows; the admin list (no draft filter) is worst.
fix: Batch the relation reads: fetch all locales/media/keywords/servers/bundles for the full client-id set in one query each (e.g. WHERE client_id = ANY($1)) and assemble in memory; fold keyword titles into the keyword query with a JOIN on catalog_keyword_locales instead of a per-keyword lookup.

title: update_client orphans the previously-provisioned bundle when the build's slug changes
detail: link_owned_bundle resolves the owned bundle from the NEW effective_slug (slug or explicit bundleSlug) and find-or-creates it, then re-points catalog_clients.bundle_id. If an admin renames a build's slug (or changes bundleSlug), the bundle previously provisioned under the OLD slug is neither renamed nor deleted; its row, its bundle_artifacts, and its on-disk builds/{oldSlug}/ tree are orphaned with no admin surface to clean them (the design doc itself notes there is no Bundles page). delete_client correctly cascades, but the update-rename path leaks.
fix: On update, detect when the effective slug differs from the client's current bundle slug and either rename the existing bundle (slug + on-disk dir) instead of provisioning a new one, or delete the now-unreferenced old bundle via delete_owned_bundle after re-link. Capture the old bundle_id before re-linking and tear it down if it became unreferenced.

title: upsert_scan never deletes artifact rows for files removed from the build → stale rows linger after re-upload
location: crates/bundles/src/repo.rs:276-293 (upsert_scan) and the comment at repo.rs:276 claiming it 'Replace[s] all artifact rows'
detail: upsert_scan only upserts the scanned set; rows for files that disappeared between scans are left in bundle_artifacts. The manifest regen (regenerate_manifest:475-516) filters entries by on-disk existence so the served manifest is correct, but the DB accumulates stale rows that show in the admin BundleWithArtifacts view and in files_count-adjacent logic, and validate()'s missing list will keep flagging them. The doc comment overstates the behavior ('Replace all').
fix: Before/after upsert_scan, delete bundle_artifacts rows for this bundle whose relative_path is not in the new scan set (e.g. DELETE ... WHERE bundle_id=$1 AND relative_path <> ALL($2)). Or run the whole replace in a transaction: delete-all-then-insert. Also correct the doc comment.

title: ingest_archive extracts ZIP over existing files without clearing the build dir → leftover files from a prior upload persist
location: crates/bundles/src/admin.rs:188-206 (ingest_archive) -> crates/bundles/src/archive.rs:36-111 (extract_zip writes into existing files_root)
detail: upload_archive ensures the build dir then extracts straight into files_root without removing prior contents. A second ZIP that no longer contains a file leaves the old file on disk (and, via scan_directory, it gets re-added as an artifact). Combined with BUG-6, the net effect is that a re-upload is additive, not a replace — contrary to the usual 'upload a new build ZIP' mental model. validate() will report these as orphaned/tracked but there's no automatic reconciliation.
fix: If the intended semantics are a full replace, clear files_root (delete_build_files then ensure_build_dir, or remove only files/) before extraction, and pair with a full artifact-row replace. If additive is intended, document it; either way make scan+rows consistent with disk.

title: delete_request_logs_older_than binds days as f64 into '($1 * interval ...)' — fractional/locale-safe but type-fragile
detail: delete_request_logs_older_than takes days: i64 but binds `days as f64` into `now() - ($1 * interval '1 day')`. Postgres multiplies double precision * interval which works, but the signature/usage mixing i64->f64 is needlessly fragile and differs from the analytics pattern which interpolates a vetted literal interval. Not a security/correctness break (param is bound), just an inconsistency that could surprise. Low risk.
fix: Bind days as i64 and use `now() - make_interval(days => $1)` (or `($1 || ' days')::interval`), or keep f64 but make the parameter type explicit. Mainly a clarity/consistency fix.

title: Catalog percent_decode drops a final byte for truncated %X escapes and mishandles edge index
location: crates/catalog/src/query.rs:31-59 (percent_decode), specifically the `b'%' if i + 2 < bytes.len()` guard
detail: The condition `i + 2 < bytes.len()` is off-by-one for the *last* valid escape: for input ending in '%XY' where '%' is at index len-3, i+2 == len-1 which satisfies `< len` (OK), but for '%X' at the very end (incomplete) it correctly falls through. The real issue is only a malformed/edge query like a trailing '%' could yield a slightly wrong decode; since this only affects the optional locale= param it is cosmetic, not a security issue (no SQL is built from it). Including for completeness given the audit scope.
fix: Use a vetted percent-decoder (e.g. percent-encoding crate) for query values, or change the guard to `i + 3 <= bytes.len()` for clarity and add a test for trailing-partial-escape inputs. Low priority.

title: Cookie parsing duplicated four times across core + admin
detail: The identical `split(';') -> split_once('=') -> trim` cookie-extraction logic is copy-pasted in four places (three private `cookie_value` in core, one public `read_cookie` in admin). Likewise `session_token` (Bearer-then-cookie) is duplicated between auth/mod.rs:192-197 and request_log.rs:255-260, and `session_token_from_headers` (the public version) is a third near-copy. Any change to cookie handling (e.g. quoted-value support, case-insensitivity) must be made in 4 spots.
fix: Add one `pub fn cookie_value(headers: &HeaderMap, name: &str) -> Option<&str>` in core::auth and have csrf.rs, request_log.rs's private copy, and admin/cookies.rs::read_cookie all call it. Collapse request_log.rs::session_token to call the existing core::auth::session_token_from_headers (already public and exported). Low risk: pure refactor, behavior-identical, covered indirectly by existing auth tests.

title: resolve_ip duplicated between the two server middlewares
detail: Both middlewares implement the same 'ConnectInfo peer first, else first hop of X-Forwarded-For' IP resolution; reqlog returns String, ratelimit returns IpAddr, but the parsing/precedence and the trusted-proxy caveat comment are identical. Two copies of a security-sensitive resolution (which hop to trust) can drift.
fix: Extract a single `fn client_ip(connect_info: Option<&SocketAddr>, headers: &HeaderMap) -> Option<IpAddr>` into a small `server/src/ip.rs` (or core) and have both middlewares format/use its result. Each has its own unit tests that would still pass. Low risk.

title: Media on-disk helpers duplicated verbatim between catalog and textures
detail: `revision_hex` (6-byte hex), `write_file` (mkdir parent + write), and `unlink_quiet` (NotFound-tolerant remove with the same warn! message) are byte-for-byte identical in both crates' store.rs. Both are 'static asset under a storage root with a cache-busting revision' stores.
fix: Add a tiny shared fs/storage helper module in core (e.g. core::storage with revision_hex/write_file/unlink_quiet) and have both crates re-use it. Catalog already depends on core; textures already depends on core. Low risk, no behavior change. (Lower priority than DUP-1/2 since these don't carry security/precedence logic.)

title: Analytics write seam (record_event) is stranded in admin crate and dead in production
detail: `record_event` is the ONLY writer to `user_events`, but it lives in the `admin` crate, which the dependency graph forbids any domain crate (network/yggdrasil/catalog) from depending on. So the documented 'domains emit events off their hot paths' can never happen: its only callers are admin_api.rs tests. `POST /users/bootstrap` bumps an in-memory counter (metrics.bootstraps) but writes no `user_events` row, so `GET /admin/analytics/timeseries` (and the dashboard 'bootstraps' graph) render empty forever. This is a real seam in the wrong crate, not just unused code. (Matches docs/audit-2026-06-14 A1/A6.)
fix: Move the event-write primitive down into `core` (e.g. core::analytics::record_event or a method on AppState) so network/yggdrasil can call it (spawn off the hot path) on bootstrap/register; keep the READ aggregation in admin. Alternatively, if the redesign's request_logs-based dashboard supersedes user_events, delete record_event + the user_events read path + migration-dependent code as dead. Medium risk (touches hot paths if wired); decide write-vs-delete first.

title: delete_owned_bundle is a dead public re-export
detail: `delete_owned_bundle` (pool-based: bundle_slug_by_id + delete_bundle_row + remove_bundle_dir) is exported from the crate root but has zero callers. The catalog's delete_client (catalog/src/admin.rs:288-338) deliberately does the delete INSIDE its own transaction using the tx-capable parts (bundle_slug_by_id + delete_bundle_row) and removes the dir post-commit, so the pool-based convenience wrapper is never used. The doc comment in lib.rs:24-35 still advertises it as the reusable entry point.
fix: Delete `delete_owned_bundle` (repo.rs:185-196) and drop it from the lib.rs re-export list + its mention in the module doc, keeping only the tx-capable parts that are actually used. Low risk: prove-dead is done (no callers in crates/). Aligns with the repo's aggressive-dead-code-removal preference.

title: is_unique_violation re-implemented in four crates/handlers
detail: The generic `matches!(err, sqlx::Error::Database(db) if db.is_unique_violation())` predicate is copied in friends, invites, and catalog/admin; identity.rs has a related constraint-name variant. Same with `map_fk`/foreign-key checks. These are trivial but proliferate the same sqlx-error pattern matching.
fix: Add `core::error::is_unique_violation(&sqlx::Error) -> bool` and `is_foreign_key_violation(...)` (or a `SqlxErrorExt` trait) and replace the three identical copies. Keep identity.rs's constraint-name-specific helper as is (it inspects db.constraint()). Low risk.

title: Public-URL origin/suffix parsing implemented twice
detail: Both parse `config.yggdrasil.public_url` by locating '://' and splitting scheme/authority/path: textures extracts the origin (scheme+authority) to absolutize texture URLs; server extracts the path suffix to mount the yggdrasil router. They split the same string at the same boundary for complementary halves, in two crates, with their own ad-hoc index math.
fix: Add a single `core::config` helper that parses public_url once into (origin: Option<String>, path: String) (or expose both on YggdrasilConfig). Textures uses .origin, server uses .path-suffix. Both have unit tests that would carry over. Low-medium risk (shared parsing must satisfy both callers' edge cases: bare origin, path-only, /api fallback).

title: Network domain (largest, most stateful) has the weakest test coverage
detail: The network crate owns the most complex stateful logic in the system — friend-request auto-accept, friend-of-friend re-validation at admission (join_requests.rs:389-395, invites.rs:302-308), the atomic capacity gate (relay.rs:222-240 try_admit_player), presence effective-status collapse, and the relay rendezvous/pipe — yet it has a single integration test file and no unit tests on its pure helpers (e.g. presence::effective_status, the FriendPresence guest-world derivation in presence.rs:303-307, relay::classify). Subtle policy regressions (e.g. a host_only flip not revoking an outstanding FoF invite) would go uncaught.
fix: Add unit tests for the pure functions first (effective_status timeout boundary, classify frame disposition, the guest_world_id->InWorld mapping) — they need no DB. Then extend network_api.rs integration coverage for the FoF re-validation-at-accept branches and the capacity race. Medium effort, low risk; raises confidence in the riskiest crate.

title: Server router composition (CORS, security headers, mount layout) is untested
location: crates/server/src/main.rs:90-194 (build_router, with_security_headers, build_cors); crates/server has no tests/ dir
detail: Only the pure yggdrasil_api_suffix helper has unit tests. The actual composition — CSP/HSTS/X-Frame scoping to the /admin subtree only, the wildcard-vs-credentials CORS branch (build_cors:253-286), the /api grouping that avoids overlapping nests, and NormalizePathLayer trailing-slash trim — is exercised by no test. A regression that, say, leaks CSP onto binary file responses or combines credentials with Any origin would not be caught here.
fix: Add a tests/router.rs using tower::ServiceExt::oneshot against build_router(state) with a test pool: assert security headers present on /admin/* and absent on /textures/*, and assert the credentials/origin CORS matrix. Medium effort (needs a DB-backed AppState like the other integration tests). Low risk.

title: N+1 query patterns in catalog DTO assembly and network list endpoints
location: crates/catalog/src/repo.rs:317-330 (list_clients loops build_client_dto, each issuing ~6 sub-queries incl. per-keyword keyword_title at repo.rs:199-206); crates/network/src/join_requests.rs:357-361 & invites.rs:97-101 (per-row build_*_dto, each doing 2-3 fetch_user_dto round-trips)
detail: list_clients does one query then, per client, separate queries for locale/media/keywords/servers/bundle — and keyword titles are fetched one-by-one inside client_keywords. Similarly join-request/invite list handlers call fetch_user_dto per row (2 user lookups each). At MVP catalog/list sizes this is fine, but it scales as O(rows x relations) of DB round-trips.
fix: For catalog: batch the locale/media/keyword/server reads with WHERE client_id = ANY($1) and group in Rust, or use JSON aggregation in one query per relation. For network lists: join the requester/host user columns into the list query (the friends search at users.rs:176 already shows the inlined-EXISTS pattern). Medium effort; flag as low-priority until list sizes grow. Low risk if done behind existing integration tests.

title: set_published interpolates a table name; pattern reused for ad-hoc dynamic SQL
location: crates/catalog/src/admin.rs:356-380 (set_published, format!s {table}); also catalog/repo.rs builds SELECTs via format!(CLIENT_COLS) and admin/requests.rs+analytics.rs format interval/bucket literals
detail: Several places build SQL via format! with internal-literal interpolation (table names, column lists, interval/bucket allowlist values). Each is individually safe (the interpolated values are fixed code literals or allowlisted, never user text, and the code comments say so), but the pattern is spread across catalog and admin with the safety argument re-derived each time. A future edit could pass a non-literal into one of these by mistake.
fix: No urgent change. Optionally centralize the windowed-analytics interval/bucket resolution (already shared via resolve_window) and document the 'only-fixed-literals' rule in one place; consider an enum for the publishable tables so set_published can't be called with an arbitrary &str. Low risk, mostly hygiene. Do NOT mechanically rewrite to query! macros (the project deliberately uses runtime sqlx).

title: User model carries #[allow(dead_code)] full-row mirror; several columns never read in Rust
location: crates/core/src/models.rs:56-80 (User with #[allow(dead_code)]: e.g. account_type, xuid, client_id, avatar_url, skin_hash partially, first_seen_at, yggdrasil_validated_at)
detail: User mirrors every users column so SELECT * mappings stay complete, gated by a crate-wide #[allow(dead_code)]. That's a reasonable choice for FromRow completeness, but it hides genuinely vestigial fields (e.g. yggdrasil_validated_at — grep shows no reader) behind the blanket allow, so a real dead column can't be distinguished from a deliberately-mirrored one.
fix: Keep the mirror, but audit which fields are truly never read (yggdrasil_validated_at, possibly avatar_url) and either remove the column/field if the schema agrees, or add a one-line comment marking it as 'mirrored-only, intentionally unread'. Low risk; do this only after confirming no migration/external consumer relies on the column. Low confidence on which specific fields are safe to drop without schema review.

Per the task framing this is the known repo-wide rustc-1.95 phenomenon, not a logic issue — but unlike the rest of the repo these specific lines actually fire today.

title: Two near-identical effective-status presence reads in different network modules
detail: Both fetch (status, last_heartbeat_at) for a user_id from presence and run it through effective_status with the configured timeout; they differ only in the row type tuple vs struct. join_requests duplicates what presence already exposes.
fix: Have host_effective_status delegate to presence::effective_status_for(state, host_id) (already pub in the same crate). One-line change, removes the duplicate query. Low risk; covered by existing join-flow tests.

title: No global 401 handler: expired session never redirects, just spams error toasts
detail: useSession resolves 401/403 to null only at the auth/me query; staleTime is 60s and refetchOnWindowFocus is disabled. The queryClient only declines to RETRY on 401 — it never clears the session or redirects. When the admin-session cookie expires mid-session, isAuthenticated stays true on the stale `me` data, RequireAuth keeps the app mounted, and every mutation/query returns ApiError(401) surfacing a per-hook toast. The user is stuck seeing repeated '...failed' toasts with no path back to login until 60s + a navigation refetch happens. There is no interceptor in apiFetch that, on 401, invalidates authKeys.me / clears the cache.
fix: In apiFetch (or a wrapping layer), on res.status===401 for any non-login call, call queryClient.setQueryData(authKeys.me, null) + queryClient.invalidateQueries({queryKey: authKeys.me}) (or a global QueryCache onError) so RequireAuth redirects to /login. Alternatively add a QueryClient `mutationCache`/`queryCache` onError that detects ApiError 401 and resets the session.
area: admin-ui SPA (security + bug audit): api client, auth/session, react-query mutations/invalidation, pages (Builds/BuildDetail/Users/Textures/Logs/Dashboard), file manager, version cascade, media flows, forms/dialogs

title: MoveDialog: stale `selected` across opens lets you confirm a move the list itself disables
location: admin-ui/src/features/builds/MoveDialog.tsx:66-145 (state at 66, confirm gate at 135-136); used by admin-ui/src/features/builds/BuildFilesTab.tsx:599-622
detail: MoveDialog stays mounted in BuildFilesTab and holds `selected` internally with no reset when `open` toggles or `sourcePaths` changes. Each destination row is disabled via disabledFor()/isSelfOrDescendant(), but the confirm button is gated only on `selected === null`. Flow: pick destination B for source A, cancel; reopen for source B (e.g. right-click folder B → Move to…). `selected` is still 'B', which is now self/descendant of the new sources so its list row renders disabled, yet 'Move here' is enabled and calls onMove('B'), attempting to move B into itself. The backend rejects (4xx) so no data corruption, but the UI offers an action it has visibly greyed out, and a stale pre-selection can also silently target a wrong folder.
fix: Reset selection when the dialog opens or sources change: add useEffect(() => { if (open) setSelected(null); }, [open, sourcePaths]); and disable the confirm button when the current selection is disabled: disabled={pending || selected === null || disabledFor(selected)}.
area: admin-ui SPA (security + bug audit): api client, auth/session, react-query mutations/invalidation, pages (Builds/BuildDetail/Users/Textures/Logs/Dashboard), file manager, version cascade, media flows, forms/dialogs

title: Unhandled promise rejection in dialog submit handlers (mutateAsync without try/catch)
detail: Both onSubmit handlers `await createUser.mutateAsync(...)` / `await resetPassword.mutateAsync(...)` with no try/catch. react-hook-form 7.54 handleSubmit re-throws errors from an async onValid callback, so on a failed mutation the promise returned to the form's DOM submit handler rejects unhandled (React does not await it) → an 'Uncaught (in promise)' console error. The mutation's onError still fires a toast so the user sees feedback, but the console error is noise and can trip error-monitoring. (UserRowActions.run() shows the correct pattern with try/catch.)
fix: Wrap the awaited mutateAsync in try/catch (swallow — the hook's onError already toasts), e.g. `try { const user = await createUser.mutateAsync(...); setCreated(user); } catch { /* onError toasts */ }`. Same for ResetPasswordDialog (only call onOpenChange(false) inside the try after success).
area: admin-ui SPA (security + bug audit): api client, auth/session, react-query mutations/invalidation, pages (Builds/BuildDetail/Users/Textures/Logs/Dashboard), file manager, version cascade, media flows, forms/dialogs

title: Concurrent multi-file upload: parallel requests on one mutation with racey pending/invalidation
detail: uploadFiles iterates files and calls uploadFile.mutate(...) once per file against a single useUploadFile instance. This fires N parallel POSTs; uploadFile.isPending (and the toolbar's uploadPending) only reflects the latest call, so the busy/spinner state is wrong, and each onSuccess independently runs invalidateBuild (N manifest-regen-triggering invalidations / N success toasts). Parallel writes + manifest regeneration on the same bundle can race or partially apply depending on backend serialization.
fix: Upload sequentially (await each before the next) or add a dedicated multi-file endpoint; gate the toolbar's busy state on the whole batch and emit a single summary toast. At minimum, disable further uploads while a batch is in flight.

title: Build Details form does not re-seed after server-side normalization on save
detail: BuildDetailsTab seeds form state once via useState(() => buildToForm(build)). The panel wrapper uses key={build.id}, which only remounts when the build identity changes — not when the same build's data changes after a successful PATCH invalidates the admin clients list. If the backend normalizes any field (e.g. slug casing, derived versions) the form keeps the user's submitted values, diverging silently from persisted state until navigating away and back. Same applies if the build is mutated elsewhere (file ops update bundle summary but not these fields).
fix: Either reset the form from `build` after a successful update (e.g. in updateClient onSuccess via a controlled reset, or a useEffect syncing on a server-version/updatedAt token), or include build.updatedAt in the panel key so a real server change reseeds.

title: ClientMediaSection silently shows empty slots on media fetch error
detail: useClientMedia error state is never handled: `const rows = media.data ?? []`. On a failed media GET the section renders as if the build has no media (all empty upload slots, empty screenshots), inviting the admin to re-upload media that may already exist. Only isLoading is handled.
fix: Add a media.isError branch rendering an error/retry state (mirror BuildFilesTab's error EmptyState with query.refetch()), distinct from the genuinely-empty case.

title: Unused mutation hooks (dead code)
detail: useAttachMedia, useDeleteKeyword, useUpdateServer, useDeleteServer, and useMoveFile are exported/defined but consumed nowhere in the SPA (verified by grep). Beyond being dead weight, useDeleteKeyword/useDeleteServer also only invalidate keywords()/servers() and NOT clients(), so if wired up later they would leave a deleted keyword/server stale on attached builds' relation arrays.
fix: Remove the unused hooks (per the repo's aggressive dead-code policy). If any are intended for future use, at minimum fix useDeleteKeyword/useDeleteServer to also invalidate catalogKeys.clients() before wiring them into UI.

title: NewFolderDialog retains previous folder name on reopen
detail: NewFolderDialog stays mounted and only resets `name` inside handleOpenChange when next===true. But the parent opens it by setting state directly (setNewFolderOpen(true)), bypassing Radix onOpenChange, and on success it calls onOpenChange(false) (not handleOpenChange), so `name` is never cleared. The next 'New folder' open shows the previously typed name pre-filled. (RenameDialog avoids this by being conditionally remounted; NewFolderDialog is always mounted.)
fix: Reset name when the dialog transitions to open via an effect (useEffect(() => { if (open) setName(''); }, [open])), or conditionally mount the dialog like RenameDialog/the delete ConfirmDialog.

title: Unhandled rejection in breadcrumb root DropZone on malformed drag payload
detail: The async onDrop awaits item.getFile()/getText() and JSON.parse(await textItem.getText(DRAG_TYPE)) with no try/catch. A malformed/foreign drag payload (or a getFile rejection) throws inside the async handler; react-aria's DropZone does not catch it, yielding an unhandled promise rejection / console error. Edge case (requires a non-standard drop payload) but reachable.
fix: Wrap the onDrop body in try/catch and ignore/toast on parse failure; guard JSON.parse and validate the parsed shape (Array.isArray(payload.ids)) before use.

title: Logout: setQueryData(me, null) immediately wiped by qc.clear(), then session refetches
detail: useLogout onSuccess does qc.setQueryData(authKeys.me, null) then qc.clear(). qc.clear() removes ALL cache entries including the just-set me=null, so the active useSession observer refetches /admin/auth/me (cookie now gone → null) before RequireAuth redirects. The setQueryData call is dead, and there's a brief redundant network round-trip / possible flash of the loading spinner during sign-out.
fix: Drop the redundant setQueryData, or clear first then set me=null (qc.clear(); qc.setQueryData(authKeys.me, null);) so the redirect is immediate without a refetch.

title: useVersions v1 fallback casts a partial object to full catalog without defaulting minecraft/fabric/forge
detail: The v1-normalization path spreads `data` and defaults only java/recommended/version, then casts `as VersionsCatalog`. If versions.json is partial/empty ({}), minecraft, fabric, and forge are undefined despite the type claiming arrays/record. Currently safe only because every consumer guards (catalog?.minecraft ?? [], catalog?.forge?.[mc] ?? []); the unsound cast is a latent trap for any future un-guarded access.
fix: Default all required fields in the normalization: { minecraft: data.minecraft ?? [], fabric: data.fabric ?? [], forge: data.forge ?? {}, java: data.java ?? [], recommended: data.recommended ?? {}, version: data.version ?? 1, generatedAt: data.generatedAt ?? EMPTY_CATALOG.generatedAt }.

title: 'Purge missing' enabled before any orphan scan despite copy telling admin to scan first
detail: The Purge button is disabled only when orphanCount === 0; orphanCount is null until a scan runs (null === 0 is false), so the destructive 'Purge missing' is clickable on page load with no orphan count shown, contradicting the dialog's instruction to 'Run a scan first to see how many are affected.' The action is server-authoritative so it's not unsafe per se, but it's an inconsistent destructive affordance.
fix: Disable purge until a scan has produced a count (disabled={purgeMissing.isPending || orphanCount === null || orphanCount === 0}), or auto-run the scan before opening the purge confirm.

title: Post-create navigation to /builds/{bundleSlug} can 404 the detail page if bundle slug != client slug
detail: CreateBuildDialog navigates to /builds/${res.bundleSlug ?? trimmedSlug}, but BuildDetailPage resolves the build via useBuildBySlug which matches client.slug (NOT bundle slug) in the admin clients list. If the backend ever derives the owned bundle slug differently from the client slug, the deep link lands on 'Build not found'. Today they coincide (the test fixture has bundleSlug === slug), so this is latent rather than active.
fix: Navigate using the client slug used for matching (trimmedSlug) rather than the bundle slug, or match useBuildBySlug on both client.slug and bundle.slug.

title: AuthProvider context value recreated every render (mutation objects in deps)
detail: useMemo deps include loginMutation and logoutMutation, which react-query returns as new result objects on every render, so the memo recomputes each render and every useAuth consumer (RequireAuth, AppShell, LoginPage) re-renders on any AuthProvider render. Minor, but defeats the memo's purpose.
fix: Depend on the stable primitives actually used (session.data, session.isLoading, loginMutation.isPending, logoutMutation.isPending) and call loginMutation.mutateAsync/logoutMutation.mutateAsync inside the callbacks (they're stable), instead of depending on the whole mutation objects.

title: Tablist / radiogroup controls have no arrow-key roving focus
detail: SectionTabs uses role="tablist"/role="tab" with aria-selected, and WindowSelector/MetricSelector use role="radiogroup"/role="radio" with aria-checked. Per WAI-ARIA APG, a tablist and a radiogroup must implement arrow-key navigation with a single tab stop (roving tabindex). Here every button is independently Tab-focusable and arrow keys do nothing, so the announced role lies about the interaction model — confusing for screen-reader and keyboard users.
fix: Add onKeyDown handlers (ArrowLeft/ArrowRight, Home/End) that move focus and selection, and set tabIndex so only the active item is 0 and the rest -1 (roving). Factor this into one shared SegmentedControl component (see DUP-1) so the fix lands once.
area: Admin SPA (admin-ui/src) — code quality, accessibility, design-system consistency

title: Status / origin differentiation is hue- or brightness-only against a no-hue palette
detail: StatusBadge maps 5xx→destructive, 4xx→secondary, 2xx/3xx→outline, and UsersPage maps origin admin/yggdrasil/local to default/secondary/outline. The design tokens are explicitly monochrome (index.css comment: 'Status = monochrome … meaning carried by icon + text', destructive/success/warn are all near-identical grays). So these badges differ only by subtle background brightness and carry no icon or text label distinguishing severity/origin — a 4xx vs 2xx vs 3xx badge is visually near-identical and fails the codebase's own 'never hue-only / icon+shape+text' rule.
fix: StatusBadge: keep the number but add a small leading icon for 4xx/5xx (e.g. AlertTriangle for 5xx, exactly as FileFilesTab StatusBadge already does for failed). Origin: the text IS the label so it is acceptable, but drop the variant juggling and use a single consistent style, or add a leading dot/icon. Ensure adjacent brightness steps meet a perceivable delta.
area: Admin SPA (admin-ui/src) — code quality, accessibility, design-system consistency

title: text-faint (oklch 0.556) on card surfaces is borderline for WCAG AA small text
location: index.css:38 (--color-text-faint); used widely e.g. StatCard.tsx:49, PageHeader hints, table captions/footers
detail: --color-text-faint is oklch(0.556 0 0) used for captions/hints on --color-card (0.205) and surface-1 (0.205). The contrast ratio is roughly 4:1 — under the 4.5:1 AA threshold for normal-size text (these are 11-12px captions). It is used pervasively for secondary information (hints, 'refreshing…', page counts, SHA cells).
fix: Bump --color-text-faint to ~oklch(0.62 0 0) (or reserve it for >=14px/600 weight 'large text' only and use --color-text-mute (0.708) for small captions). Verify with a contrast checker against card (0.205) and surface-1.
area: Admin SPA (admin-ui/src) — code quality, accessibility, design-system consistency

title: Three near-identical segmented controls
detail: WindowSelector and MetricSelector are byte-for-byte the same pattern (inline-flex rounded-md border border-edge bg-surface-1 p-1 + active bg-surface-3 text-text-hi else text-text-mute hover:text-text), differing only in role and option labels. SectionTabs is the same visual with role=tab. This is the same component three times with divergent a11y (see A11Y-1) and divergent paddings (px-2.5 py-1 vs px-3 py-1.5).
fix: Extract one <SegmentedControl items value onChange ariaLabel mode='tabs'|'radio'> that owns the shared styling + roving keyboard nav, and have all three call sites use it. Removes ~80 lines and centralizes the A11Y-1 fix.
area: Admin SPA (admin-ui/src) — code quality, accessibility, design-system consistency

title: Empty/loading/error table-state patterns are implemented two different ways
location: pages/BuildsPage.tsx:146-232 (SkeletonRows + inline empty TableRow); vs pages/UsersPage.tsx:127-149 & pages/TexturesPage.tsx:204-226 (TableSkeletonRows + TableStateRow)
detail: Users and Textures consistently use the shared components/shared/TableStates.tsx (TableSkeletonRows, TableStateRow) for loading/error/empty. BuildsPage instead hand-rolls a local SkeletonRows component and an inline empty-state TableRow with bespoke markup — and notably has NO error state at all (if useAdminClients errors, the table just renders empty 'No builds yet', which is misleading). This is an inconsistency a user will feel: the same page family renders empty/error states differently.
fix: Delete BuildsPage's local SkeletonRows and inline empty block; use TableSkeletonRows/TableStateRow like Users/Textures, and add an isError branch with TableStateRow(icon=AlertCircle) so a load failure is distinguishable from genuinely-empty.

title: Pagination footer duplicated verbatim between Users and Textures
detail: The entire footer (count text with 'Loading…'/'refreshing…' logic + 'Page X of Y' + prev/next icon buttons with identical disabled logic) is copy-pasted, differing only in the noun ('users' vs 'skins/capes'). Any change (e.g. adding a page-size selector or fixing the disabled-when-isError case) must be made in two places.

title: StatCard duplicated as StatCardDisplay
detail: StatCardDisplay is a copy of StatCard whose only difference is it renders a preformatted string instead of value.toLocaleString() (and drops the value===0 mute styling). The card shell, skeleton, header/description/icon layout, and hover:border-edge-md are identical.

The two empty-chart-state helpers (DashboardPage EmptyChartState and TrafficSection EmptyChartState) are also identical — extract one shared component.

title: KeywordsSection and ServersSection are large near-duplicates
detail: Both sections share the same structure: attached-chips/list with remove, a Select of available items + Add button, a 'Create new' toggle, and an inline create form with pending state and attach-on-create. ~330 lines with the attach/detach/create/pending wiring duplicated; the only real differences are the entity fields (keyword slug/title vs server slug/name/address) and chip vs list rendering.
fix: Extract a generic <AttachableEntitySection> taking the entity's hooks, the list of attached items, an availability filter, and a render-create-fields slot. Even a shared 'AddExistingPicker' (Select + Add + Create-new toggle) sub-component removes the bulk of the duplication.
area: Admin SPA (admin-ui/src) — code quality, accessibility, design-system consistency

title: Build Details form grid is non-responsive (grid-cols-2 with no breakpoint)
detail: The Details form is hard-coded to 2 columns at every width, while the rest of the app is carefully responsive (sm:/lg:/xl: grids everywhere, e.g. Dashboard STATS, media slots). On a narrow viewport the Slug/Title/version selects get cramped into 2 columns with no single-column fallback. The Switch row uses sm:col-span-2 implying a responsive intent that the container never honors.
fix: Change to `grid grid-cols-1 gap-4 sm:grid-cols-2` so it collapses to one column on small screens, matching the rest of the app's breakpoints.
area: Admin SPA (admin-ui/src) — code quality, accessibility, design-system consistency

title: Skeletons use bg-accent which is lighter than the surfaces they sit on
location: components/ui/skeleton.tsx:9 (`bg-accent`); --color-accent oklch(0.269) vs --color-card oklch(0.205) in index.css:46,56
detail: Skeleton renders bg-accent (0.269) which is brighter than card (0.205) and surface-1 (0.205). Placeholder skeletons reading brighter than the real content they replace is visually backwards (placeholders should read as muted/recessed). Note BuildFilesTab.tsx:471-478 separately uses bg-surface-1 animate-pulse for its skeleton, so even the skeleton fill is inconsistent across the app.
fix: Set Skeleton fill to a recessed token (e.g. bg-surface-2 or a dedicated --color-skeleton at ~0.23) and use the shared Skeleton in BuildFilesTab instead of the bespoke bg-surface-1 blocks.
area: Admin SPA (admin-ui/src) — code quality, accessibility, design-system consistency

title: Data tables lack zebra striping / sticky header, hurting scanability of dense rows
detail: Tables rely solely on hover:bg-muted/50 row highlight and a single header border. For the long, dense, monospace-heavy tables (request logs, textures, users) there is no row banding and the header does not stick on scroll, so it is easy to lose the column a value belongs to. This is the highest-density surface in a monochrome UI where rows already blend together.
fix: Add optional even:bg-surface-0/40 zebra striping (a TableRow variant or a Table `striped` prop) and a sticky header (sticky top-0 bg-card z-10 on TableHeader) for the scrollable log table. Keep it subtle to honor the dark language.
area: Admin SPA (admin-ui/src) — code quality, accessibility, design-system consistency

title: Card default border uses border-edge while interactive cards hover to border-edge-md — base cards look flat
detail: Card's base border is border-edge (white/0.1) which is very faint on the canvas; combined with shadow-sm (barely visible on dark) the cards read as nearly borderless panels. Stat cards add hover:border-edge-md, but static content cards (ManifestPanel, media, traffic charts) stay at the faint border, so the elevation/grouping of the page reads weakly.
fix: Bump Card's resting border to border-edge-md (0.15) for a clearer panel edge on the dark canvas, or pair the faint border with a real elevated surface (bg-surface-1) rather than relying on shadow-sm which is near-invisible at this contrast.
area: Admin SPA (admin-ui/src) — code quality, accessibility, design-system consistency

title: Decorative section icons in chart/card titles are aria-hidden but several status icons inside badges are not labeled
detail: Most icons are correctly aria-hidden or paired with text. But the Badge icons (Pencil for Draft, EyeOff for Hidden, CheckCircle2/AlertTriangle/Loader2 in the files StatusBadge) sit next to text so they are fine for sighted users, yet the Loader2 'Processing' spinner conveys a live state with no aria-live, and the 'Hidden' eye-off badge's meaning depends on the icon. These are minor but inconsistent with the otherwise careful aria-hidden discipline.
fix: Ensure icon+text badges keep the text as the accessible name (they do) and add aria-live="polite" to the processing StatusBadge container so the status transition is announced. Low effort, rounds out the a11y story.

title: No code-splitting — recharts and all routes ship in one eager bundle
location: src/App.tsx:1-12 (static page imports); src/main.tsx; vite.config.ts (no manualChunks / no rollup chunk config); components/ui/chart.tsx:2 (`import * as RechartsPrimitive from "recharts"`)
detail: All page components are statically imported in App.tsx and recharts (a heavy charting lib, the single largest dependency here) is pulled into the main chunk via chart.tsx even though charts only appear on Dashboard and Logs. react-aria-components (used only by the file manager DnD) is likewise always loaded. The initial bundle therefore carries recharts + react-aria + every page for what is often a quick admin login.
fix: React.lazy + Suspense the route components in App.tsx (especially DashboardPage, LogsTrafficPage, BuildDetailPage which pull recharts/react-aria), so recharts splits into a route chunk. Optionally add a manualChunks entry isolating recharts. This is the highest-leverage perf change.
area: Admin SPA (admin-ui/src) — code quality, accessibility, design-system consistency

title: Unused exports: ChartLegend, ChartLegendContent, ChartStyle (public), AvatarImage, duplicated window type
detail: ChartLegend and ChartLegendContent are never imported anywhere (no chart uses a legend); ChartStyle is exported publicly but only used internally. AvatarImage is exported but the only Avatar usage (AppShell) renders AvatarFallback only — no image source is ever supplied, so AvatarImage is dead. TimeseriesWindow (WindowSelector.tsx) and TrafficWindow (shared/types/logs.ts) are two structurally-identical `"24h"|"7d"|"30d"` types; LogsTrafficPage even feeds a TrafficWindow into WindowSelector which is typed for TimeseriesWindow (works only by structural typing).
fix: Per the repo's aggressive-dead-code rule: drop ChartLegend/ChartLegendContent and un-export ChartStyle from chart.tsx (these are vendored shadcn, so confirm no planned legend first); keep AvatarImage only if avatars will get images, else remove it; unify the two window types into one (export the shared TrafficWindow and have WindowSelector consume it).

title: Pervasive /// doc comments conflict with the repo's why-only comment rule
location: 124 `///` comments across 25 files, e.g. features/builds/FileList.tsx:21-37,39-40,55-58; FileContextMenu.tsx:20-43; SelectionToolbar.tsx:5-7; logsTraffic/StatusBadge.tsx:12; TrafficSection.tsx:420-421
detail: The user's standing rules are 'default to NO comments; only why-comments for genuine workarounds/invariants' and 'remove decorative comments on every pass'. Many of the `///` blocks are descriptive/what-comments (e.g. 'The contextual action bar shown while one or more entries are selected', 'HTTP status code rendered as a class-coloured badge', 'Like the dashboard StatCard, but renders a preformatted string') rather than why-comments. Some ARE legitimate why-comments (the Radix Forge remount note in BuildDetailPage:452-459, the ring-buffer key note in LiveLogsSection:161) and should stay.
fix: On the next pass, delete the descriptive/what `///` comments and keep only the ones explaining a non-obvious why (Radix remount workaround, ring-buffer key, NONE/CUSTOM sentinels, selection-is-artifact-only invariant). This is a hygiene sweep, not urgent.

title: TexturesPage tabs mix icon and no-icon items causing label misalignment
location: pages/TexturesPage.tsx:80-83 (TABS: Skins has icon Shirt, Capes has none)
detail: The SectionTabs TABS array gives 'Skins' a Shirt icon but 'Capes' no icon. In the same tab strip one label sits flush-left while the other is inset by the icon+gap, so the two tabs are visually misaligned. Either both should have icons or neither.
fix: Give Capes an icon too (e.g. a cape/flag glyph) or drop the Shirt icon from Skins so the strip is uniform.

title: AppShell logo title uses both text-h2 (carries weight) and font-bold redundantly; nav active relies on bg + weight only
detail: Minor: text-h2 already sets font-weight 600 via the token (index.css:124-126), so font-bold is a redundant override (and slightly fights the type scale). Separately, active nav state is conveyed by bg-accent-soft + font-semibold + text-hi; there is no aria-current on the active NavLink, so assistive tech is not told which nav item is current (NavLink supports it but it is not wired).
fix: Drop the redundant font-bold (or use text-h1 if a bolder logo is wanted intentionally). Add `aria-current="page"` to the active NavLink (react-router's NavLink can set this via the className callback's isActive or by passing the prop).

title: FileList `selectable` uses a verbose boolean ternary and FileGrid omits the download-once column with no parity note
location: features/builds/FileList.tsx:156 (`entry.artifact !== null && !entry.isDir ? true : false`); FileGrid.tsx (no download-once affordance)
detail: `x ? true : false` is a lint smell — it is just `entry.artifact !== null && !entry.isDir`. More substantively, FileViewProps declares onToggleDownloadOnce and FileList renders a Switch for it, but FileGrid accepts the same props yet never exposes download-once, so the two views are not feature-equivalent — a user toggling view mode loses an action with no indication. Minor prop-quality/consistency issue.
fix: Simplify the boolean expression. Decide whether grid view should also surface download-once (e.g. in the card footer or only via context menu) and document the intentional divergence, or drop onToggleDownloadOnce from FileGrid's destructure since it is unused there (FileGrid currently doesn't even destructure it, so it is silently dead in that path).

title: Inconsistent dialog body spacing: some forms use gap-4 flex, others mt-4/mt-6 manual offsets
location: pages/users/CreateUserDialog.tsx:161 (flex flex-col gap-4) vs pages/BuildsPage.tsx:99-119 (mt-4 space-y-4 + mt-6 footer) vs NewFolderDialog.tsx:66,76 (mt-4 + mt-6) vs MoveDialog.tsx:91,124 (mt-2 + mt-4)
detail: Dialog internals space their header/body/footer with three different conventions: a single gap-4 flex column (Create/Reset user), manual mt-4 body + mt-6 footer (Builds/NewFolder/Rename), and mt-2/mt-4 (Move). DialogContent already provides gap-4 between its direct children, so the manual mt-* values are both inconsistent and partly redundant, producing slightly different vertical rhythm per dialog.
fix: Standardize on the DialogContent gap (wrap form bodies in a flex flex-col gap-4 and drop the mt-4/mt-6 offsets), or codify a single spacing convention and apply it to all dialogs for consistent rhythm.
